articles.title: Parents of nurse killed by ICE demand DOJ release evidence of fatal shooting
articles.summary: The parents of Alex Pretti, the ICU nurse and U.S. citizen who was killed in Minneapolis said they were “begging” the Justice Department “to do what is right.”
articles.body: The parents of Alex Pretti, a U.S. citizen and ICU nurse who was fatally shot by immigration officers in Minneapolis nine months ago, slammed the federal government and demanded the release of all the evidence related to their son’s death. Michael and Susan Pretti said at a news conference Tuesday that the federal government has kept them in the dark for 275 days — even after they sent a letter to Attorney General Todd Blanche over the summer “begging for basic information the law affords,” including the identities of the officers involved in the shooting. “At every turn, they have ignored us, misled us and shielded Alex’s killers,” Michael Pretti said. “We want our son’s killers to be brought into justice once and for all,” Susan Pretti said. “We are here begging for the Department of Justice to do what is right.” Kiersten Pels, a spokesperson for the Department of Justice, told NBC News that communications between federal officials and victims’ families “do not typically occur” during an investigation. “As is standard practice, communications with family members, if any, come at a later stage of a case, such as indictment, initial appearance, plea, trial, or sentencing,” Pels said in a statement. “The timing is consistent with how these types of investigations proceed.” The Department of Homeland Security referred all questions to the FBI. Tuesday’s news conference comes nearly a week after Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty said the federal government stopped sharing information with Minnesota authorities who are investigating Pretti’s killing. Moriarty’s office sued the Trump administration in March to compel federal officials to share key evidence pertaining to Pretti’s death and the shootings of Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis, a Venezuelan man who was wounded by an ICE officer, and Renee Good, who was fatally shot by another ICE officer. The three Minnesota shootings took place in January, after the Trump administration deployed more than 3,000 immigration officers and agents to the state as part of “Operation Metro Surge,” the DHS’s largest immigration enforcement operation. In July, Minnesota officials said the federal government was starting to turn over evidence in the cases, including police body camera video and hard drives containing statements. Moriarty said at the time that she expected to receive “all the evidence.” That changed this month, according to Moriarty. In a statement last week, she accused the federal government of withholding evidence related to the fatal shootings of Good and Pretti and “obstructing our investigations for however long they can.” “Our lawsuit was filed to gain access to all of the evidence and our efforts to obtain it will continue. We have filed our motion for summary judgment to bring an end to the case and secure the evidence to which we’re entitled,” Moriarty said. “The federal government responded with a motion to dismiss; their aim is clear.” In the motion filed by DOJ attorneys at the U.S. District Court in Washington, D.C., last week, the federal government argued it has the authority to decline sharing information with state authorities if no formal legal proceedings are underway. The Trump administration has previously suggested that state prosecutors have no jurisdiction to investigate federal officers, while Minnesota officials have said the federal government can’t be trusted to investigate itself. “This is not normal. This is not justice. It is morally wrong,” Michael Pretti said at the news conference. He decried that the lack of cooperation between federal and local authorities in investigating his son’s killing “is just baffling, disappointing and reprehensible.” Steven L. Schleicher, a lawyer for the Prettis who was also at the news conference, said his clients are entitled to see any evidence about the shooting under the Crime Victims Rights Act. “How is it possible that the Department of Justice is not sharing evidence,” Schleicher said. “What are they hiding?” During his confirmation hearing in July, Blanche was asked about his commitment to sharing information on the ICE-involved shootings in Minnesota with state officials. He said he expected the investigations into those cases to be run as usual, adding that “the definition of full cooperation can be disputed.” Videos showing Alex Pretti’s killing haunt his family every day, his parents said. At the same time, according to them, those images were crucial in contradicting the Trump administration’s narrative of the shooting. “The federal government went on TV and lied about Alex. They tried to slander his memory to cover up their crime,” Susan Pretti said. “Not only was it wrong, it was shameful, unfair, unacceptable. We want to clear our son’s name.”

articles.title: Dutch zookeeper dies after being mauled in leopard enclosure
articles.summary: The woman began her career at the park when she was 17 and had worked there on-and-off for four decades.
articles.body:
An experienced keeper at a Dutch zoo has died days after being mauled in a leopard enclosure, the safari park has confirmed.

The woman, who had worked at Beekse Bergen park for 40 years, was caring for two Persian leopards in an indoor facility when she was attacked on Saturday.

She sustained injuries to her head and neck and had emergency surgery, but the park confirmed her death on Tuesday.

An independent investigation will be launched into the incident, it added in a statement.

Announcing her death, Beekse Bergen - in the south of the Netherlands - said the keeper began her career there when she was 17 and had worked there on-and-off for four decades.

"Her passing has deeply affected us all, and our hearts go out to her family, friends, and loved ones. At this moment, our primary focus is on supporting her family and her colleagues," the statement added.

The two leopards, which are usually kept away from staff, had been brought inside due to bad weather conditions.

It is not clear exactly what happened in the enclosure because there are no CCTV cameras inside.

Local news website NL Times reported that despite her injuries she managed to alert colleagues via her walkie-talkie. She was then taken to hospital in a helicopter in a critical condition.

A park spokesperson told Omroep Brabant, a local media outlet, that the leopards were behaving naturally and they would not be euthanised.

Beekse Bergen said it would create a memorial location for guests and staff members to share their condolences.

articles.title: Chris Mason: Budget needs to go some way towards delivering PM's promises
articles.summary: Support on the cost of living, and in particular energy bills, as well as announcments on devolution will be central to John Healey's first Budget.
articles.body:
Two quotes from the chancellor and the prime minister get to the heart of this Budget.

"The money New Labour had in the 90s is simply not there now….Britain has it harder now," the Chancellor, John Healey, said last month.

And from Andy Burnham, days before he became prime minister: "This change...is the most significant change moment in our politics for 40 years."

So what happens when the economic realities confront the political ambitions of this new government?

As Helen Miller, director of the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS), puts it : "We have a relatively new government with seemingly big ambitions but facing a long list of constraints.

"Some of those constraints…are self imposed, others are being worsened by global events, most noticeably war in the Middle East."

Let's be clear, plenty in Westminster in all parties will say that the amount of money around isn't everything – how well taxpayers' money is spent and where it is spent matters too.

And spending less and taxing less, plenty argue, should be a priority.

But in the bones of many in the Labour Party is an instinct that the government, the state, can and should be a vital agent in driving change and improvements in people's lives – a worldview grounded in a sense that governments should proudly step in, rather than one that believes they should get out of the way.

And how do you deliver a proudly proactive state, delivering for people in a noticeable way, when the tax burden is generationally high, the national debt is sky high, energy bills are rising and inflation is higher than expected?

Minimum wage set to rise but 18-20 year-olds will not get bigger increase

Tax on banks, energy bill help and minimum wage rise - what could be in the Budget?

Healey's Budget needs to sustain the stronger economy through gathering clouds

But ministers argue all of this doesn't mean the government is powerless.

Many are expecting support on the cost of living, and in particular energy bills, to be targeted at the most vulnerable. The banks are braced for a levy or surcharge that may pay for this.

There will be an announcement about further spending on defence, but not yet how spending 3% of national income on our security will be delivered by 2030 – that will come in next year's Spending Review.

And one of the prime minister's key ideas - handing power away from Westminster and closer to you, devolution - will be central too.

There will be, the chancellor told BBC Newscast, a "really radical devolution of powers and resources to local leaders that are often better placed to get beyond the departmental systems."

But some at Westminster fret extra money for mayors and others in local government are not yet accompanied by adequate checks and balances to ensure that money is well spent.

The chancellor will argue the economy is becoming more robust – and yes, there are some economic indicators that are more positive than forecast: growth is better than expected, as is productivity and unemployment is down.

But as the Resolution Foundation think tank points out : "John Healey's problem is that conflict in the Middle East has once again pushed up energy prices and interest rates.

"So, despite the signs that the UK economy is becoming more resilient, household and public finances are in for another shock."

Four ways Labour could raise money in the Budget without hiking income tax

Chris Mason: Jackdaw approved but tricky energy trade-offs remain

In essence, we can expect a smaller Budget this time, compared to some in recent years, when it comes to the scale of tax and spending changes.

The chancellor has been talking up a desire to offer "breathing space" and "hope" - a tacit acknowledgement that there is a limit to what the government can do given the constraints it faces.

It has promised not to raise income tax, national insurance or VAT, a self imposed constraint, as the IFS put it. And there are the international ones beyond its control too.

The big question for many will be whether the Budget is – or can be - big enough to meet the moment? Opposition parties will argue it amounts to tinkering.

The government will try to convince you it is one of many moments in the coming weeks and months that will attempt to deliver the scale of change the prime minister has promised.

articles.title: Utah grovels to Pat McAfee, WNBA’s brunch game is peak stupid & why you should take your dogs on vacation
articles.summary: Campaign text messages, Pat McAfee's war with Utah, and the WNBA's absurd 12:30 p.m. Finals tip-off all highlight this edition of "Nightcaps."
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. One week until Election Day. Now, don't you go clicking away on me. You did not accidentally stumble upon a column about politics and who you should vote for and what's at stake, blah blah blah. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE No, I'm just here to gripe about something that seems to be a new phenomenon this midterm season: campaign text messages. Look, I know that if you sign up for a candidate's text messages, you will get inundated with a steady stream of pleads for donations. But I would never sign up for something like that. So tell me why I get a dozen text messages a day from various state and local politicians — attacking their opponents, begging for my vote, detailing BS stories about how they grew up in a middle-class family where "nothing came easy" and they learned the "real value of a hard day's work." Delete. Report spam. Every time. Look, voting is important, and we should all do it. I'm glad to live in a country where we actually get a say in who's making our laws and affecting our quality of life. But unsolicited campaign text messages should be illegal. Not to mention they just feel like bad practice. How do you think bombarding me with an endless string of text messages will somehow endear you to me? It actually makes me not want to vote for you. Is everyone dealing with this right now? Is this a new thing or have I somehow just managed to avoid the onslaught until this campaign season? November 3 truly can't come soon enough. Next Tuesday, we party. But until then, let's do some Nightcaps. Pat McAfee is at war with the University of Utah Wow oh wow, College GameDay was AWKWARD on Saturday. It all started with that girl who was chosen for the kicking contest. Now, admittedly, I love the kicking contest. Every Saturday, I yell to my husband, 'It's time for the kick!' and we run into the living room to watch. This Saturday, I knew it was doomed from the start. As soon as I saw the contestant. Now, don't get me wrong. I'm all about girl power. I am, after all, a girl. And I have no doubt there are plenty of women who can kick a 33-yarder. Soccer players obviously come to mind. But the last couple of times they've had women competing, they've been women with the athleticism of a potato. This isn't an anti-woman thing. Obviously. Plenty of men have missed, too. But if you — either gender — know you have an absolutely 0% chance of nailing this kick, why even put your name in the raffle? Why embarrass yourself like that? And to make matters worse, she had the gall to tell Pat McAfee he should be giving her $3 million to make the kick — not the $1 million she was already offered. Girl. My skin is crawling with awkwardness. Anyway, we found out yesterday there was a lot more under the surface about GameDay’s trip to Utah that we didn’t see. Before the show, Utah’s official social media account posted a video of students doing impressions of Pat, including one calling him "corny" and another saying his shirtless bit was "creepy." Pat said he had no problem with random students roasting him, but he did have a problem with the university itself amplifying it right before he was about to go on national TV and promote their school. He said the whole thing made him feel "very, very uncomfortable," especially given the very real safety threats he and other public figures face, and even referenced the Charlie Kirk assassination while explaining why it bothered him. By the end of GameDay, Pat picked Houston to beat Utah and told the crowd, "I’ll never see you again, hopefully." Utah has since apologized, saying the post was meant to be lighthearted but "missed the mark," and that Pat and the GameDay crew are always welcome back. Something tells me Pat will not be taking them up on that invitation anytime soon. But what do we think, guys? Was Pat being dramatic? Or is Utah insufferable? Or both? While we're on the topic of insufferable, though ... The WNBA's brunch game is perfect for this very dumb league There’s an old saying that goes something like: "A lack of preparation on your part does not constitute an emergency on mine." Someone should print that out and tape it to the front door of WNBA headquarters. Because Game 6 of the WNBA Finals — a game in which the Golden State Valkyries could literally WIN THE CHAMPIONSHIP — will tip off Thursday at 12:30 p.m. ET. That is 9:30 IN THE MORNING for Golden State fans. Hope nobody scheduled a Zoom meeting. Here’s how we got here: The Atlanta Dream normally play at the 3,500-seat Gateway Center, but they wanted their Finals games at the much larger State Farm Arena, home of the Atlanta Hawks. The problem is State Farm already had conflicts on every single Atlanta Finals date, including a Hawks-Cavaliers game Thursday night. The league managed to shuffle Games 3 and 4 around those conflicts, but somehow got all the way to a guaranteed Game 6 before figuring out what the hell to do with this one. And listen, I understand wanting the bigger arena. But I also understand planning ahead, which apparently no one bothered to do. The Hawks were always scheduled to play Thursday. This did not sneak up on anybody. Yet now EVERYONE has to move heaven and earth because the Dream doesn’t want to play the biggest game of its season in its actual home arena. FROM ANTHEMS TO DEFINITIONS, THE WNBA KEEPS DOING DUMB THINGS, AND THE REASON FOR IT WILL LEAVE YOU SPEECHLESS The Hawks pushed their game back an hour. State Farm Arena employees have to flip the building between games. Broadcast partners have to rearrange programming. Staff, security, vendors, parking attendants and fans all have to adjust. And the Valkyries’ fan base gets to watch a potential championship celebration on their office laptops while pretending to answer emails at 9:30 a.m. Pacific. Warriors coach Steve Kerr was asked about the situation and joked that it was better than playing at the YMCA in front of 75 people. He also said he’ll be watching over breakfast. Which, honestly, sounds lovely. I do love a good brunch. Unfortunately, I’m not sure my boss is going to let me pop a bottle of champagne and start hammering mimosas at my desk because the WNBA scheduled a potential championship game before lunch. But wait! It gets better. Because the Hawks need the arena later that night, ESPN’s Ramona Shelburne reported that if Golden State actually clinches the championship Thursday, there may not be enough time for a proper celebration on the State Farm Arena floor. So they could have to move the party to a practice court. Imagine that. You win the first championship in franchise history, confetti falls, everybody cries, you lift the trophy … And then someone comes over the PA: "Congratulations, ladies. Now please grab your belongings and clear the floor. The Hawks have shootaround." What an absolute clown show. Par for the course. Let's open the mailbag. 📩 Email: amber.harding@outkick.com (Send your thoughts, stories, tips, rants and photos of your dog.) 🐦 Twitter/X: @TheAmberHarding 📸 Instagram: @amberharding Giving the people what they want: Rocky Drew in Katy, TX writes: I saw this on Instagram and thought about all of the places that Rocky gets to see. I have not seen Rocky pictures in a while or other dog photos/videos for that matter. It's like you are conforming to the Nightcaps sports standard. We need dogs and other animals at least once per week to break up the monotony. Tell the boss that I said so. Amber: Ask and you shall receive. Fortunately, my boss is very pro-dog. These are some photos from Rocky's adventures the last couple of weekends. We have hit that sweet spot of perfect fall weather here in the South, and the hiking is glorious. articles.title: In 2020, a Michigan couple agreed to buy a $1.275 million home for their growing family, but the seller cited his ex-wife's name on the title; after a $1.55 million judgment against the buyers, an appeals court overturned it
articles.summary: A Michigan appeals court has overturned a $1.55 million (£1.19 million) judgment against a couple who backed out of buying a luxury home after discovering
articles.body: A Michigan appeals court has overturned a $1.55 million (£1.19 million) judgment against a couple who backed out of buying a luxury home after discovering that the seller did not have sole ownership of the property. In an unpublished opinion under docket number 373967 (Roger Lewis and Nicole Susser v. Robert Blumberg), the Michigan Court of Appeals set aside the trial court's decision. The three-judge panel found that the trial judge had made serious legal errors involving jury instructions and the use of settlement discussions as evidence. The legal dispute began in November 2020, when Roger Lewis and Nicole Susser looked to buy a new home for their growing family.Agreement signed for Franklin Village propertyOn 22 November 2020, Mr Lewis and Ms Susser signed a binding agreement to buy a home in Franklin Village, Michigan, from owner Robert Blumberg for $1,275,000. Under the agreement, the buyers paid earnest money into an escrow account. However, title searches carried out before the sale was completed uncovered an unexpected legal issue with the property's ownership. Court documents filed with the Michigan Court of Appeals showed that public land records still listed Mr Blumberg's former wife as having an ownership interest in the property. Because her interest was officially recorded, Mr Blumberg could not transfer clear ownership on his own. His former wife would also need to take part in the sale and sign the property transfer documents.Disputed closing and trial court judgmentAfter discovering the ownership issue, the buyers raised concerns about whether the seller could legally transfer full ownership by the agreed closing date. The parties disagreed over how to resolve the title problem, and their communications broke down. Mr Lewis and Ms Susser eventually stopped the purchase and asked for their deposit to be returned. This led both sides to bring competing claims before the Oakland Circuit Court. After a civil trial in the Oakland Circuit Court, a jury ruled in favour of Mr Blumberg on his counterclaims. The trial court then issued a final judgment ordering Mr Lewis and Ms Susser to pay $1.55 million in damages for breach of contract. The buyers filed further motions asking the court to change the amount awarded and temporarily stop enforcement of the judgment. After the circuit court rejected their requests, the couple appealed to the state appeals court.Appellate panel identifies trial errorsThe Michigan Court of Appeals panel included Presiding Judge Michael F. Gadola, Judge Colleen A. O'Brien, and Judge Philip P. Mariani. After reviewing the trial record, all three judges agreed to overturn the lower court's decision. The appeals court found that the trial judge had made a serious legal error by allowing the jury to hear protected settlement discussions. Under Rule 408 of the Michigan Rules of Evidence (MRE 408), statements made during settlement talks generally cannot be used to prove or disprove legal responsibility or the validity of a disputed claim. "We agree," the appeals panel stated in its opinion. It found that allowing this evidence had unfairly harmed the buyers' case and prevented them from receiving a fair trial. The court also found problems with the instructions given to the jury about real estate contracts. The opinion explained that when a property seller refuses in advance to complete an agreed sale, or fails to provide a title that can legally be transferred without unresolved claims, the buyer may be excused from completing the purchase. "As has long been recognized, when a seller of land anticipatorily repudiates an agreement for its sale, '[t]hat refusal . . . to perform excuse[s] performance by the [purchaser] and excuse[s] tender of performance by the [purchaser],'" the panel wrote, citing established Michigan real estate law.Judgment reversed and remandedThe Court of Appeals concluded that the $1.55 million judgment against Mr Lewis and Ms Susser could not stand because the trial court had applied the evidence rules incorrectly and failed to give the jury important instructions about the seller's obligations regarding property title. The appeals court overturned the Oakland Circuit Court's damages judgment in full and sent the case back to the trial court for further proceedings in line with its legal findings.You use AI every day. articles.title: Karan’s unbeaten 162, Mavi’s fifty lift UP against Puducherry
articles.summary: Karan Sharma’s unbeaten 162 and Shivam Mavi’s 50 lifted Uttar Pradesh to 328/9 at stumps on Day 2 vs Puducherry in Ranji Trophy.
articles.body: Lucknow: Karan Sharma’s superb unbeaten century and Shivam Mavi’s valuable half-century lifted Uttar Pradesh into a strong position after a shaky start against Puducherry on the second day of their Ranji Trophy match at Siechem Stadium in Puducherry on Tuesday. At stumps, Uttar Pradesh were 328 for 9 after 121 overs.Resuming at their overnight score of 67 for 4 after 37 overs, with Karan on 17 and Aaradhya Yadav on 2, Uttar Pradesh added 25 runs for the fifth wicket before Aaradhya (15) was dismissed by Udeshi.After his departure, Zeeshan Ansari (19) shared an important 42-run sixth-wicket partnership with Karan off 96 balls before falling to Ankit Sharma at 128 for 6. Shivam Mavi then came in at No. 7 and made a major contribution. He and Karan added a crucial 87 runs off 164 balls for the seventh wicket. Returning to action after injury and rehabilitation, Mavi struck a fine 50 off 88 balls, including five boundaries and a six, before being dismissed by Karan Kannan at 215 for 7 in 86.3 overs.After Mavi’s dismissal, Kartik Yadav joined Karan, and the pair added 39 runs for the eighth wicket before Kartik, who made 16, was dismissed by Udeshi at 254 for 8 in 99.6 overs. Tailender Yash Dayal then contributed 3 runs and supported Karan in a 52-run ninth-wicket partnership off 94 balls before he, too, was dismissed by Udeshi at 306 for 9 in 115.4 overs.Karan Sharma played a magnificent innings, remaining unbeaten on 162 off 328 balls, with 13 fours and six sixes.Speaking to TOI, Karan Sharma said, “We were focused on building a big partnership. Zeeshan and I were shaping one nicely, but he got out. Even then, I put together a substantial stand with Shivam Mavi, which helped us reach a good total. Tomorrow as well, our aim will be to avoid losing wickets and put up a big score.” Meanwhile, UP coach Gyanendra Pandey said, “Karan Sharma played a superb innings, and his partnership with Mavi helped put up a strong total. articles.title: Cruise vacation comes to crashing halt as ship slams into 2 cargo vessels
articles.summary: The Mein Schiff 3 collision in Bremerhaven, Germany, damaged lifeboats and forced TUI Cruises to cancel the entire Canary Islands cruise for shipyard repairs.
articles.body: A luxury cruise ship slammed into two cargo vessels during stormy weather in Germany and abruptly brought a planned trip to the Canary Islands to an end. The incident took place in Bremerhaven, Germany, Sunday as the Mein Schiff 3 was departing the port. TUI Cruises confirmed the incident to Fox News Digital and said no passengers were injured. ANGRY CRUISE PASSENGERS SAY FRUSTRATING ISSUE SHOULD HAVE BEEN DISCLOSED BEFORE BOOKING "As a result, we have decided to cancel the planned cruise to the Canary Islands," the spokesperson said. "We very much regret having to take this step." Technical teams and experts inspected the ship shortly after the collision. They determined it would need repairs at a shipyard, a TUI Cruises official told Fox News Digital. The collision was reported by Bremen Police on Sunday evening. Officials said the cruise ship collided with two container ships during stormy weather before returning to Columbus Quay. OUTRAGED CRUISE PASSENGERS SOUND OFF ABOUT 'IMMENSE DISAPPOINTMENT' AFTER ABRUPT CANCELLATION "According to current knowledge, no one was injured in the collision," the translated police statement said. "Information on the exact extent of the damage and the cause of the accident is not yet conclusively available." Footage posted to Reddit appears to show a view from the cruise ship during the collision, with at least one person shouting as the vessel scrapes against a cargo ship, damaging lifeboats along its side. Bremen police said they're investigating the collision. Police also reportedly opened an administrative offense investigation into the captain of the Mein Schiff 3, according to German broadcaster NDR. THOUSANDS BOOKED TROPICAL BAHAMAS CRUISE AND ENDED UP IN FREEZING CANADA INSTEAD The TUI Cruises spokesperson said the safety of passengers and crew remains the company's "top priority." "We believe this is the only responsible decision and the right course of action to maintain our high safety standards," the spokesperson said. "Our focus now is on keeping our guests fully informed." "Our focus now is on keeping our guests fully informed, supporting them and assisting them with the next steps." The incident and video prompted discussion online, with users expressing sympathy for affected passengers. "Ooof. That looked expensive," another chimed in. One Reddit commenter claimed to have been aboard another cruise ship in Bremerhaven that was scheduled to depart shortly after the Mein Schiff 3. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS "I'm actually on a different cruise ship in Bremerhaven that was supposed to leave shortly after Mein Schiff 3 last night," the user wrote. "Shortly before we were supposed to leave, they announced the port was closed. It was really windy." The commenter said his or her ship had originally been scheduled to stop in Hamburg but was diverted because of the weather. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "I can't see the damage but Mein Schiff 3 is docked back in port," the Reddit user added. "I can see it from the bridge cam." Other cruise vacations have faced similar disruptions in recent months. Passengers aboard a Royal Caribbean cruise ship were left scrambling earlier this year after their seven-night Alaska voyage was abruptly canceled due to technical problems. articles.title: Flavio Bolsonaro headed to the US after losing Brazil election, sources say
articles.summary: SAO PAULO, Oct 27 (Reuters) - Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro has left the country for the United States after losing Sunday's presidential election and r...
articles.body:
SAO PAULO, Oct 27 (Reuters) - Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro has left the country for the United States after losing Sunday's presidential election and refusing to comply with a Supreme Court order to hand over ‌his passports, three sources said.

The US Embassy in Brazil did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Bolsonaro's lawyer also ‌did not respond.

Bolsonaro's location was not immediately clear. One source who is close to the Bolsonaro family said Flavio had arrived in the United States, but declined to say ​where.

The source said US President Donald Trump's administration had granted asylum to Flavio and his immediate family. Trump has previously alleged Flavio's father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, was a victim of judicial persecution in Brazil.

Flavio's departure threatens to deepen a rift between the two most populous nations in the Americas. Leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has accused Washington of colluding with the Bolsonaros to put them back in power, and Reuters reported ‌ahead of Sunday's election on a US State ⁠Department campaign to restore them to office.

The elder Jair Bolsonaro also went to the United States after refusing to concede to Lula in 2022, when former US President Joe Biden was in office. He eventually returned to ⁠Brazil but was later given a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after his supporters stormed government buildings in Brasilia.

Trump made no mention of Flavio Bolsonaro's departure in comments to the press on Monday, but said the Brazilian vote "looked like another rigged election."

Lula's office did not respond to a request for ​comment.

Bolsonaro ​was favored to win Sunday's presidential election but ended up losing in a ​shock result to Lula.

On Monday, he was given 24 hours ‌to surrender his passports as part of a money laundering probe in which he denies wrongdoing, but his documents were canceled after the deadline lapsed, two other sources said.

Bolsonaro, who loses his immunity from prosecution when his Senate term ends in February, said on Monday he had no plans to flee.

"I have never thought about leaving the country," he said. "I will hand over my passports and defend myself against this travesty, which is a clear attempt to intimidate me."

Brazil's Minister of Institutional Relations Jose Guimaraes commented on reports of Bolsonaro leaving the country in ‌an interview with CNN Brasil.

"I have no confirmation from the Federal Police or ​oversight bodies," he told the news outlet. "But this speaks a lot about our opponent's ​lack of preparation to govern the country."

Senator Bolsonaro has ​yet to officially concede defeat — saying on Sunday he would seek the annulment of the result over alleged ‌voter irregularities — but his Liberal Party said on Monday ​it acknowledged Lula's victory.

It remains unclear how ​Bolsonaro was able to leave the country while he was facing a 24-hour deadline to hand over his passports. A senior Federal Police official said Bolsonaro had not exited the country via any regular migration point.

Eduardo Bolsonaro, Bolsonaro's younger brother who lives ​in the United States, said ahead of the vote ‌that an election loss would require a move.

"If my brother does not win, I'm in favor that he would leave ​the country," he told podcaster Steven Crowder this month.

(Reporting by Ricardo Brito and Luciana Magalhaes; Additional reporting by Lucinda ​Elliot, Brendan O'Boyle Oliver Griffin; Editing by Gabriel Stargardter and Aurora Ellis)
